policy.store: individual source-stated financial facts with a citation and a short DISI paraphrase (<= 400 characters); never publisher text
never_store: values inferred from nearby years or league-wide tiers without a Dodgers statement
a post-trade pool nobody printed (no arithmetic)
a disagreeing report whose resolution has not been reviewed
policy.pages_read: Every source below was fetched once (HTTP 200) and parsed as raw HTML by the author of this migration (not through a summarising fetch tool). MLB.com pages answered HTTP 406 and True Blue LA HTTP 403; neither is used and nothing was worked around.
policy.precision_rule: Same as Migration 030: a figure printed with every digit is EXACT; a figure printed in rounded form is ROUNDED with the precision of its last stated digit; 'approximately' is APPROXIMATE and never selects a canonical value.

environment_reports.note: MLB Trade Rumors calls $2.9MM the Dodgers' 2012-13 spending pool.
MLB Trade Rumors, July 2, 2013, says the Dodgers had a pool of $2,112,900 when the Marmol slot trade was made.
Dodgers Digest, July 3, 2014, says the Dodgers have $1,963,800 to spend on international bonuses.
Baseball America's December 2016 listing places the Dodgers in the $4.75 million tier; a tier label, not an itemised allotment. In-period trades were not checked.
Baseball America lists the Dodgers in the $5,348,100 pool group for 2020-21; trading was prohibited.
MLB Trade Rumors, January 15, 2021, lists the Dodgers among twelve teams that can spend $5,348,100.
Baseball America lists the Dodgers' 2021-22 pool as $4,644,000. This is the effective allocation after the Bauer penalty, not a pre-penalty base.
MLB Trade Rumors lists $4,644,000 as the Dodgers' (and Blue Jays') lowest allotment for 2021-22; effective post-penalty allocation.
MLB Trade Rumors says the Dodgers lost $500K of their pool for signing Trevor Bauer. Memo only: the stored pool already reflects it, so it must not be subtracted again.
